hero.lead: A nation of 3.4 million with farmland across eight tenths of its land and almost all its power renewable, whose sustainability-linked bond ties the cost of borrowing to climate and native forest targets.

register.name: Nominal peso and US dollar bonds
register.detail: Ministry of Economy and Finance · issued 28 July 2026 · peso bond due 2035 reopened at 7.75% (US$1,298 million) · US dollar bond due 2037 reopened at 5.356%, 75 bps over US Treasuries (US$399 million) · demand of up to US$3,353 million
register.note: Budget-wide; US$447 million of the total went to exchanges and buybacks of shorter bonds
register.text: International issuance equivalent to US$1,697 million, reopening a fixed-rate nominal peso bond due 2035 and a US dollar bond due 2037. Investors could pay in part with shorter peso, inflation-indexed and dollar bonds, which the Ministry says extends the average maturity of the debt and reduces refinancing risk. It funds the budget as a whole and is not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Sovereign sustainability-linked bond
register.detail: Ministry of Economy and Finance · priced 20 October 2022 (US$1.5bn) · reopened November 2023 (US$700 million) · due October 2034 · coupon 5.75% · fourth annual report, 29 May 2026
register.note: Greenhouse gas intensity was 48% below 1990 in 2024, against a 2025 target of at least 50%
register.text: A US dollar bond whose coupon rises or falls by 15 basis points on each of two targets: the intensity of greenhouse gas emissions and the area of native forest maintained. The fourth annual report finds native forest fully maintained against its baseline on the latest assessment, of 2021, and the 2025 observation will decide any change in the coupon. It ties the cost of the nation’s borrowing to measured climate and nature results.

register.name: Global peso bond due 2035 and US dollar bond due 2037
register.detail: Ministry of Economy and Finance · priced 22 October 2025 · new fixed-rate nominal peso bond due 2035 at 8% (US$1,350 million equivalent) · US dollar bond due 2037 reopened at 4.73%, 78 bps over US Treasuries (US$500 million) · demand of up to US$3,835 million
register.note: Budget-wide; the peso bond was issued at the lowest rate since Uruguay entered the international markets, the Ministry says
register.text: International issuance equivalent to US$1,850 million: a new nominal peso bond at a fixed rate and a reopening of the US dollar bond due 2037, with up to US$100 million of the peso bond used to exchange shorter peso bonds. It funds the budget as a whole and is not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: US dollar global bond due 2037
register.detail: Ministry of Economy and Finance · priced 7 February 2025 · coupon 5.442% · 100 bps over US Treasuries · repaid in three annual payments, 2035 to 2037 · US$1.2bn for cash, the rest to buy back bonds due 2027 and 2031 · orders of up to US$5.4bn from more than 234 accounts in 28 countries
register.note: Budget-wide; the lowest spread Uruguay has paid on a new US dollar global bond, the Ministry says
register.text: A new US dollar bond with an average life of 11 years, issued together with a tender offer for the bonds due 2027 and 2031. It funds the budget as a whole and is not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Strengthening Competitiveness, Private Investment and Employment
register.detail: World Bank · approved by the Board 14 September 2026 · variable spread · repayable in 6.5 years with 2.5 years of grace · with a Deferred Drawdown Option for rapid liquidity in economic shocks
register.note: Budget-wide; the reforms include the formal hiring of young people, women and vulnerable groups
register.text: World Bank financing for reforms to promote private investment, create more and better jobs and strengthen fiscal sustainability, among them the ratification of the trade agreement with the European Union, simpler customs procedures, wider access to finance for firms and new fiscal rules. Its measures on the formal hiring of young people, women and vulnerable groups bear on the livelihood standard.

register.name: Green and Resilient Growth Development Policy Loan
register.detail: World Bank · Board approval announced 17 November 2023 · interest reduced by up to US$12.5 million if livestock methane intensity per unit of product falls at least 33% in 2028 to 2032 and at least 36% in 2033 to 2037
register.note: The first World Bank loan to link its financing terms to ambitious environmental targets, the Bank says
register.text: Budget support for reforms toward a more sustainable economy, including incentives to conserve native forests. Its interest cost falls if Uruguay meets verified targets for the methane intensity of its livestock, assessed each year from 2028. It funds the budget as a whole and is not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Cerro Largo solar photovoltaic park, UTE
register.detail: CAF loan to UTE, guaranteed by the Republic · draft contract approved by the Executive 10 August 2026 · 16 years with 78 months of grace · SOFR plus 1.80%
register.note: UTE, the state electricity company, is the borrower and the executing agency
register.text: A CAF loan to UTE, the national electricity company, to build a solar photovoltaic park in the department of Cerro Largo, with the Republic as guarantor. It adds solar power to a grid that is already mostly renewable and serves the energy standard.

register.name: Contingent liquidity credit line
register.detail: CAF · approved by the Executive 23 July 2026, published 17 August 2026 · up to US$750 million for 7 years · first loan of up to US$180 million at SOFR plus 1.50%, 7 years with 24 months of grace
register.note: Budget-wide; the first loan backs the public debt management plan
register.text: A contingent, non-revolving and non-committed liquidity credit line from CAF for the Ministry of Economy and Finance, with a first loan of up to US$180 million to support the plan for managing the public debt. It funds the budget as a whole and is not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Más Barrio credit line
register.detail: CAF · approved by CAF’s Board 16 December 2025 · framework agreement approved by the Executive 25 May 2026 · loans of up to 18 years with up to 72 months of grace, guaranteed by the Republic
register.note: Approved the day CAF announced US$980 million for four projects in Uruguay, among them vulnerable communities
register.text: A credit line from CAF for the Más Barrio programme, for the infrastructure and housing works the programme needs and for regularisations and relocations. CAF says its December 2025 financing for Uruguay will support the transformation of vulnerable areas. It serves the shelter standard.

register.name: Casupá dam, OSE
register.detail: CAF loan to OSE · signed 22 May 2026 · a dam on the Casupá stream in Florida storing 118 million m³ · works expected to begin in early 2027 and end in the third quarter of 2029
register.note: Fresh water reserves for the metropolitan system are to rise from 80 to 200 million m³
register.text: A loan from CAF to Obras Sanitarias del Estado (OSE), the state water company, to build the Casupá dam, which is to strengthen the water security of the Montevideo metropolitan system and help avoid shortages like those of 2023. CAF also provides technical support. It serves the water standard.

register.name: Water Resources and Solid Waste Policy Reform Support Programme II
register.detail: IDB loan 6067/OC-UR · approved by the IDB 29 October 2025 · contract approved by the Executive 27 March 2026 · one tranche · 19.5 years with 72 months of grace
register.note: The Debt Management Unit records US$100 million from an IDB policy-based loan in January to July 2026
register.text: A policy-based loan from the Inter-American Development Bank, the second of its programme, that supports reforms in water resources and solid waste; the Ministry of Economy and Finance executes it. It serves the water standard.

register.name: Innovation to Support the Energy Transition and Climate Action, stage I
register.detail: IDB loan 5931/OC-UR · programmatic policy-based loan with a deferred drawdown option · draft contract approved by the Executive 2 December 2024
register.note: The amount is not stated on the resolution page
register.text: The first stage of a programmatic policy-based loan from the Inter-American Development Bank, with deferred drawdown, for innovation in support of Uruguay’s energy transition and climate action. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: National Care System Strengthening and Sustainability Programme
register.detail: IDB loan 5897/OC-UR and investment grant 5898/GR-UR · signed 14 October 2024 · executed by the Ministry of Social Development through the National Care Secretariat · amendment approved by the Executive 22 September 2026
register.note: The amendment adds CND and INACOOP as sub-executing agencies and leaves the essential financial terms unchanged
register.text: A loan and a grant from the Inter-American Development Bank to strengthen and sustain the National Care System, run by the Ministry of Social Development. Care for people who depend on others bears on the health and livelihood standards.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Power from water, wind and sun already flows; every new connection can be clean.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 17.9% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.

items.name: The Land
items.label: Land area, 2023
items.text: Territory to farm, power and protect.

items.name: FUCVAM
items.text: The federation of Uruguay’s mutual-aid housing cooperatives, founded in 1970, whose members build their own homes and hold them for their use value rather than their market value; 332 of its cooperatives had been built and were lived in across Montevideo in December 2024, and the model counts more than 80,000 inhabitants.

items.name: Estación Óptica
items.text: An optician in Tacuarembó that refurbishes donated eyeglass frames and gives them to people who cannot obtain them, and turns the plastic lenses that opticians normally throw away into teaching materials for the city’s public schools and kindergartens; it won second prize among small firms in the Uruguay Circular Award 2025.
items.source: Ministry of Industry, Energy and Mining, 2025

items.name: ELdeS
items.text: A Uruguayan start-up with the first interactive platform to learn Uruguayan Sign Language with artificial intelligence, used in public schools, cooperatives, companies and agencies, which donates one licence to an educational or social institution for every licence it sells and was among ten ventures recognised by the National Agency for Research and Innovation at the Premio NOVA 2025.

items.name: Kaur
items.text: A Uruguayan impact start-up that reuses hotel textiles to make clothing, creating jobs for women in vulnerable situations and promoting responsible consumption in fashion.

items.name: Coopespal NP
items.text: A cooperative of artisanal fishers in Nueva Palmira, Colonia, supported in December 2025 by the Ministry of Industry, Energy and Mining’s call for cooperative investment projects to process river fish into fillets and value-added products made from fish pulp.
items.source: Ministry of Industry, Energy and Mining, 2025
